title: ABS 2021 Census of Population and Housing, General Community Profile DataPack: Victoria's Statistical Areas Level 1, the tables of households, dwellings, tenure, rent and moves
provider: Australian Bureau of Statistics, 2021 Census DataPacks, General Community Profile (GCP), Statistical Area 1 for VIC, short headers (2021_GCP_SA1_for_VIC_short-header.zip, 101 MB): members read by range requests, without downloading the archive
credit: Source: ABS, 2021 Census of Population and Housing, General Community Profile DataPack (CC BY 4.0)
licence: CC BY 4.0 (the DataPack's Readme/CreativeCommons_Licensing_readme.txt, kept with the tables; the ABS asks that its data be attributed to it, that derived data not be, and the acknowledgement 'ABS data used with permission from the Australian Bureau of Statistics')
citation: Australian Bureau of Statistics (2022), 2021 Census of Population and Housing, General Community Profile DataPack, Statistical Area 1, Victoria, https://www.abs.gov.au/census/find-census-data/datapacks (retrieved 2026-11-05)
format: CSV, one row an SA1 (SA1_CODE_2021, 11 digits) of Victoria. G02 Selected Medians and Averages (median weekly rent and household income, average household size); G33 Total Household Income (Weekly) by Household Composition (occupied private dwellings, in bands from nil to $4,000 or more); G35 Household Composition by Number of Persons Usually Resident; G36 Dwelling Structure (occupied private dwellings by structure, and unoccupied private dwellings); G37 Tenure and Landlord Type by Dwelling Structure (owned outright, with a mortgage, rented by landlord type, other); G40 Rent (Weekly) by Landlord Type (rented dwellings in bands); G41 Dwelling Structure by Number of Bedrooms; G44 Place of Usual Residence 1 Year Ago (persons at the same or a different address). Small cells are randomly perturbed by the ABS (its TableBuilder confidentiality), so that sums over tables differ slightly.
coverage: Victoria's 15,482 SA1s at the Census of 10 August 2021, taken during a lockdown of COVID-19 when many international students were abroad: the centre's households and vacancies that night were not those of an ordinary year.
